claim: Damaged doors in the per-band underground VTT scene get two builds. V04 §5.6 (5), the home of the damage below ground, states the per-band VTT rule, and T-V4-82 (e) tests it: 'a door past its threshold no portal (an open gap)'. §11.1's underground-band clause (l. 15976-15981) had its line of sight rewritten this round (VRC2T-06). Its `portals` still sit 'at openings in a wall line — a door access, a door or breach link, an underground building's entrances, each tunnel grille (closed when locked, bricked, gated or secret)' with no damage exception. By contrast, §11.1's per-storey clause writes portals only for 'every entrance whose door that level leaves standing'. A builder of §11.1's profile writes a closed door portal at an underground building's fallen door; V04's builder writes none.
required_change: §11.1's underground-band clause: 'an underground building's entrances' → 'an underground building's entrances whose door its own decay level leaves standing (a door past its threshold an open gap, no portal; V04 §5.6 (5))'. V04's END: its §5.5 VTT row may cite the same in one clause; §5.6 (5) already states it.

At THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE the village is one district, and a disaster look ruins V07 §5.6 (3)'s units: its ends, or in an end-less thorp its toft groups. Read at a village rung, one struck end ruins and tones the whole village.
required_change: ONE FIX with VV12-r3-02 (its §8.2 and §11.2 text), and §8.6's 'A building of a district a disaster look ruins' → 'A building on a unit a disaster look ruins (§10.2 (d)'s `neighbourhoods`: a district; at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE a unit of V07 §5.6 (3) — its ends, or an end-less thorp's toft groups — on the plots `villageUnitPlots` gives it)'.

claim: R3-16 (e) rules that at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE `info.crisis.ruinedFor` is the village `WhyProvider`'s answer row, shown once. V09 §4.21.12 (4) and §5.8 now show it only from that provider. V07 §4.5 and W74 say the provider reads '§2.9's `crises` and `week` with DR44 at the viewer's key … never from the model'; its `info.village.season` and `info.village.festival` rows are likewise 'read from view state'. No interface carries a view into a why answer: §11.2's `why` member is `{ kind: 'why'; id; path?; mode?; historyPage? }`; V10 §2.13's `WhyProvider.explain(model, id, path, key, { mode, historyPage })` takes none; V10 §3.9 calls providers 'over the committed model with the caller's key'; V09's `WhyCardModel` reads `query({ kind: 'why' })` with no view; and J-V10.125 says 'a `why` section is model-side and cannot know the view's week'. These three rows' inputs have no producer (principle (7)). One builder adds a view parameter; another, following V10, cannot produce the rows, and the village card shows no crisis line — the case R3-16 (e) meant to settle.
required_change: One view-bound why at the API's home. (1) §11.2's `why` member: `{ kind: 'why'; id: Id; path?: string; mode?: 'asPlaced'|'asNow'; historyPage?: number; view?: ViewHandle /* a view-bound why: a provider whose rows state a view's look — V07 §4.5's crisis, season and festival rows — reads that view's §2.9 week, yearWeek, festival and crises and its looks evaluation (LooksAnswer) at the view's effective key; absent, no such row is given */ }`; *Knowledge* adds 'a `why` with a `view` admits its view-bound rows as `looks` does'. (2) END at V10: §2.13's `WhyProvider.explain` opts gain `view?: { week: number; yearWeek: number; festival: ViewState['festival']; crises: ViewState['crises']; looks: LooksAnswer }`; §3.9's query paragraph adds 'and, for a view-bound why, the view's state and `looks` answer'; the `why` tool passes `ClerkSession.view` where present (§3.5). (3) END at V09: §2.7's `WhyCardModel` reads `query({ kind: 'why', …, view })` with the card's view. (4) END at V07: §4.5 and W74 cite `opts.view` for the three rows.

claim: T-ER-21's outcome for the host's commands (l. 16624) reads 'the week and the selection view state that travels, the layers a logged `setLayer` — never an input', in the words adjudication-r3's note gives. §11.3, the home, says the selection is not view state: `view.set { select: ids }` selects as a user's list pick would and reports `entity.selected` — 'a command, never a stored key' — so it neither persists nor travels as `view.changed`. The bar's own fixture (byte-identical replay without the host) passes either way. A test writer checking the stated outcome would look for a travelling selection the bridge never sends.
required_change: T-ER-21's outcome: 'the week and the selection view state that travels, the layers a logged `setLayer` — never an input' → 'the week view state that travels, the selection a command (the frame selects and reports `entity.selected`; never a stored key), the layers a logged `setLayer` — never an input'.

claim: Partly fixed: §8.8 now applies an Auto change decided while the view is idle at once, and a device-pixel-ratio change at once when idle (J-A121.07; T-ER-26), but §12.5 *The frame budgets Auto holds* still reads 'a rolling p95 over the budget through 2 s steps one rung … down, one under 60 % of it through 10 s one up, each applied only at the settle and at most once in 10 s'. *The settle* is §8.8's gesture event (*Gestures*: 'the settle, at which the Auto changes decided during the gesture apply'), so a builder reading §12.5 never applies a change decided on an idle view: VRC2T-08's defect, restated in the same unit.
required_change: §12.5's clause reads '… each applied only while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise — and at most once in 10 s (§8.8's Auto loop) …'.

claim: §11.2 *At a drawn week* (new this round): 'every row, count, match and gap unit is the head index's restricted to the entities the frame holds'. A kind chip's match is 'every entity holding an admitted Use whose cls is among its classes … one match per entity' (*Find's match listing*), and a Use is itself an addressed record with `opened`/`closed` (§2.6), while V06 §3.15.2's frame is a whole model with its own uses. So at a scrubbed week (a) a building that held a smithy then and a bakery at the head is matched by 'Bakery' (the building is held by the frame) and not by 'Smithy', glowing, pinning and counting a use the frame does not draw — unless 'entities' includes the Use, which two builders read two ways; (b) a use or building the frame holds that the head has since closed, moved or demolished is in no head row and is never matched though drawn — the second half of VRC2T-07's claim, left standing against R3-24's own sentence ('Find counts, glows, pins, lists and gaps only the entities that frame holds'). T-ER-25's scrub fixtures exercise neither case.
required_change: §11.2 *At a drawn week* reads: 'where that week's frame is not the head, the listing is the frame's: the head index's matches less those whose entity, or whose matching use, the frame does not hold open at that week, plus the frame's own uses and entities of the chip's classes or target that the head lacks or holds otherwise — read from V06 §3.15.2's frame (its Use records with `opened` at or before the week and no `closed` by it; the HistoryStore images between the frame and the head) — so a building matches by its use at that week, never its head use, and an entity or use the frame holds matches though the head has since closed, moved or demolished it; a chip with none there counting 0; absent, the head'; §8.2's *At a drawn week* sentence cites it ('each chip's matches are §11.2's listing at that week'); T-ER-25's scrub fixture adds a week before a matched use closed and a building whose use changed since that week (matched by its use then; the closed use matched and drawn). V09 §4.21.10 (8) and V10's `read_map find` then read the same listing (their 'restricted to the entities that frame holds' citing §11.2).

claim: The new typed `ExportOpts` members state ranges a script or a bridged `export.request` can pass outside — `vtt.pxPerSquare` 'at least 50', `band` 'neighbourhood only for a district-sized or smaller frame', `vtt.scene` naming a building, storey or depth band, `stride` (years), `size` (`px`, `dpi`) — and nothing says what an export does with 30 px a square, the neighbourhood band over a whole town, a storey the building lacks, a stride of 0 or a zero-sized picture (clamp, refuse or draw); T-ER-19 and T-ER-20 test none. The dialog never produces such values (no normal path, hence minor).
required_change: §11.2 states beside `ExportOpts`: a member outside its range that has a nearest lawful value is clamped to it and named in the export's report (`pxPerSquare` → 50; `band` 'neighbourhood' over a larger frame → 'district'); one with none — a `vtt.scene` naming what the scope lacks, a `stride` ≤ 0, a `size` side or `dpi` ≤ 0, a zero-area `frame` — refuses the export (`export.refused` / the rejected promise, naming the member), never a crash or a hang; T-ER-19 adds a request of each.
